name: The Generative Horizon: Applied Hermeneutics, Linguistic Attractors, and the Limits of Model Self-Report
headline: The Generative Horizon: Applied Hermeneutics, Linguistic Attractors, and the Limits of Model Self-Report
description: For language-model agents, language is simultaneously an object of interpretation and a medium of generation. The represented situation formed through instructions, prior turns, retrieved records, tool results, summaries, and corrections is not merely what a model computes about; it is part of what the model computes through. This preprint calls that situated condition the generative horizon and develops recursive interpretive conditioning for cases in which retained outputs reshape later interpretation and action. It connects model self-report, reasoning-trace faithfulness, mechanistic interpretability, linguistic attractors, provenance, supersession, and epistemic engineering while preserving a strict boundary between measured representations and claims about inner observers or phenomenal awareness.

citation.name: Precise Records, Unstable Meanings: Measurement Validity and Unsupported Claims Derived from AI Agent Telemetry
